statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band well below the block threshold because the Globex session reopened at 22:00 UTC into a 21-point range with no gap, confirming the two-way, retracement-friendly structure of the completed August month-end session, while Stress stays elevated on Brent near 91 dollars, a 4.76 percent 10-year yield and roughly 62 percent implied odds of a September rate hike.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a two-sided regime in which mean reversion is functioning. The first thirty minutes of the reopened Globex session traded 29,501.25 to 29,522.50 with the September contract last at 29,507.25, a 0.02 percent move from the 29,513 reference and no gap, which is the orderly-reopen path rather than a headline-driven repricing. The cash session that preceded it closed 0.08 percent higher at 29,456.97 after traversing its full 29,304.49 to 29,483.90 range in both directions with repeatedly successful retracements. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align: crude and long-end yields rose together while the 2-year barely moved, the Dow fell 0.70 percent against a flat Nasdaq-100, megacap performance split with Tesla up 5.5 percent and Nvidia up 1.5 percent against Amazon down more than 3 percent on FTC lawsuit reports, semiconductors closed seven of seven higher, and VIX finished near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range. Iran's retaliation for the Larak Island strike was reported intercepted with no impacts at United States bases, which limits the discontinuity premium relative to an open-ended escalation. The identified conditional risks are an overnight Strait of Hormuz headline into thin Asian liquidity and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, the only forecast hour mapped to WATCH.
headline: Globex reopens flat in a 21-point range after the Nasdaq-100 closes August at 29,456.97, while Brent near 91 dollars, a 4.76 percent 10-year and hawkish September repricing keep Stress elevated
body: CME equity index futures reopened at 22:00 UTC after the daily 21:00 to 22:00 maintenance halt. The September E-mini Nasdaq-100 contract has traded a 29,501.25 to 29,522.50 range and was last at 29,507.25, 0.02 percent below the 29,513 reference, with no opening gap. That 21-point range across the first half hour is the central current observation for Tail: the reopen produced no directional impulse, no shallow-pullback chain and no extension away from the reference, so the pathological no-retracement path that would overwhelm a mean-reversion approach is not present in live evidence. The preceding cash session closed the August month-end at 29,456.97, up 23.54 points or 0.08 percent, after opening at 29,404.29 and traversing a 29,304.49 to 29,483.90 range in both directions with deep and repeatedly successful retracements. The broader tape was weaker and split: the Dow fell 374.09 points or 0.70 percent to 53,185.90, the S&P 500 fell 0.33 percent to 7,686.14 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.12 percent to 26,370.89, yet all three booked August gains, with the Nasdaq up more than 3 percent on the month. Energy remains the dominant macro channel. WTI settled around 86.22 dollars, up 2.83 percent, and Brent around 90.68 dollars, up 2.71 percent, after United States forces struck two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard responded with ballistic missiles against the King Hussein and Al Azraq air bases in Jordan and drones toward a United States-linked facility in the United Arab Emirates. Jordan's military reported intercepting eight missiles, a United States official stated there were no impacts at United States bases, and the Emirati defence ministry denied that Al Minhad was struck. CENTCOM described the Larak action as limited and precise, and Iran's president said Tehran was not seeking war. That combination of an intercepted retaliation and de-escalatory framing on both sides materially limits the geopolitical discontinuity premium relative to an open-ended escalation, and no further escalation has been reported since the cash close. Rates repriced hawkishly along the long end. The 10-year yield rose 3.8 basis points to 4.758 percent within a 4.726 to 4.768 range, the 30-year rose about 5 basis points to 5.26 percent, and the 2-year was effectively unchanged at 4.354 percent, a steepening consistent with an oil-driven inflation impulse rather than a policy-path shock. Implied odds of a September rate increase are near 62 percent, up from roughly 40 percent a week earlier, following the Federal Reserve chair's Jackson Hole remark that inflation was running too hot. Volatility did not confirm the risk-off narrative: VIX closed at 14.92, up 3.40 percent, but finished near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range, and delayed VIX futures context showed a 2.2 percent decline. Internals were split rather than aligned. Megacap performance dispersed sharply, with Tesla up 5.5 percent and Nvidia up 1.5 percent after a 3.5 billion dollar MediaTek investment, against Amazon down more than 3 percent on Federal Trade Commission lawsuit reports, Alphabet down 2.1 percent and Microsoft down 1.2 percent, leaving only three of eight tracked names higher. Semiconductors were positive across all seven tracked names with a mean gain near 1.5 percent, while Communication Services fell 1.5 percent and Consumer Cyclical fell 0.75 percent against a modestly positive Technology sector. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and raise Stress; they do not establish the persistent directional efficiency that Tail measures. Shared cross-asset context collected at 21:08 UTC was used only as delayed supporting evidence and never as live price-path evidence. Tail is therefore held at 10 in the low band, Stress eases one point to 51 in the elevated band on the calm reopen, and Confidence is 88 on continuously verified index, futures, volatility, rates, energy, geopolitical and calendar evidence gathered directly from primary sources this hour. The narrow danger window spans 13:45 to 15:00 UTC on 1 September, covering the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI Final and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings releases into an already hawkish rate backdrop. That 14:00 UTC hour is the only one of the next 24 mapped to WATCH; the remaining 23 map to EA_ON. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours run from the late Sunday Globex session through the August month-end U.S. cash close and into the maintenance halt. Published Tail opened at 9 in an orderly regime, rose to a 15 peak at the 00:00 UTC Asian repricing of the Larak Island strike, eased steadily to 5 through the European morning, spiked to 17 at 09:00 UTC on the crude-led inflation impulse, and then held a narrow 9 to 13 band across the entire U.S. session before finishing at 10. Stress climbed from 33 to a 55 peak as oil, long-end yields and September rate-hike odds repriced hawkishly, and closed at 52. Every one of the 24 hours mapped to EA_ON and green, and no hour is unavailable. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout, reflecting continuously verified levels rather than inferred structure. Dominant mode was mixed for 20 of the 24 hours, with one normal hour, one trend-down hour at the Asian repricing and two event/whipsaw hours around the 09:00 to 10:00 UTC crude impulse. The defining feature of the window is that no hour produced the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures, which is why an elevated and rising Stress track never translated into a block-band Tail reading.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the reopened Globex session through the Asian and European sessions and into the first September U.S. afternoon and close. Conditional Tail starts at 10 on the observed orderly reopen, drifts between 9 and 13 overnight with the 00:00 UTC Tokyo open as the highest overnight reading, eases to a 9 trough at the pre-European handover, firms to 12 in the 09:00 UTC hour that carried the prior session's Tail peak, and rises to a conditional peak of 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour on 1 September when ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously into an already hawkish rate backdrop. That is the only hour mapped to WATCH and yellow; the other 23 hours remain EA_ON and green, and the path decays to 9 in the closing 21:00 UTC maintenance-halt hour when no price path can form. Conditional Stress traces the same shape, easing to 48 in the halt hour and peaking at 60 in the data hour, staying in the elevated band throughout on the unchanged oil, long-end yield and Strait of Hormuz backdrop. Confidence decays monotonically from 88 to 69 with horizon, which is the normal evidence-quality gradient rather than a deterioration signal. Two identified conditional mechanisms drive the shape: an overnight Middle East headline printing into thin Asian liquidity, and delayed second-leg repricing after the 14:00 UTC data block. Neither is observed at the assessment cutoff, and every hour beyond the current one describes structure conditionally.
